summary.short: Joint resolution of the Banco Central do Brasil and the National Monetary Council implementing Open Banking in Brazil. It sets rules for sharing customer data and services, consent, authentication and interfaces for institutions authorized by the Central Bank, phased in from 1 June 2020 to 25 October 2021.
summary.long: Joint resolution of the Banco Central do Brasil and the National Monetary Council implementing Open Banking (Sistema Financeiro Aberto). It applies to financial institutions, payment institutions and other institutions authorized by the Central Bank (Art. 1). Participation is mandatory for S1 and S2 institutions for certain data and services, and voluntary for others (Art. 6). Customer consent must be specific, valid for up to twelve months unless the customer sets a longer period for successive payments, and cannot be given through adhesion contracts, pre-filled forms or presumed consent (Art. 10). Consent, authentication, confirmation and revocation steps apply (Arts. 8, 15-20). Institutions must offer standardized dedicated interfaces and must not create obstacles to sharing (Arts. 23, 28). Partnerships with non-authorized entities require prior due diligence and contract terms, including Central Bank access (Arts. 36-38). Each institution designates a responsible director, files semi-annual reports and keeps records for five years (Arts. 32-33, 49). Technical standards are set by a participants' convention subject to Central Bank approval (Arts. 44, 47). Phased deadlines run from 1 June 2020 to 25 October 2021 (Art. 55). The text sets no fine amounts; the Central Bank may veto or restrict partnerships (Art. 52).

obligations.summary: Consent must be requested in clear language, refer to determined purposes, state a validity period compatible with the purposes and limited to twelve months, identify the transmitting institution and the data or services, identify the client, and be obtained after entry into force.
